perf-mon.js — YTAF Engine Diagnostics ===================================================================== Dev-only instrumentation for the webOS YouTube mod.

WHAT IT DOES 1. Hooks every runtime boundary this mod actually crosses (JSON.parse, JSON.stringify, fetch, XHR, MutationObserver, IntersectionObserver, timers, rAF, DOM queries, layout reads, event listeners) and charges the cost back to the module + function responsible. 2. Carries a registry of every function in the codebase and its role, so the cluster reports "this is firing / this is silent / this should not be running here" instead of anonymous numbers. 3. Runs a feature-expectation sweep on every page transition: for each enabled option it knows what should happen on this page, and verifies it against live DOM and runtime evidence. 4. Renders an automotive instrument cluster sized for a TV across a room. 5. Emits machine-readable bottleneck reports for an AI agent to review.

LOAD ORDER MATTERS. Import this first in userScript.js (after the polyfills). It installs "inner" probes immediately, so it sits underneath adblock's JSON.parse hook and can time the native parse; then it arms "outer" probes in a deferred task once the bundle has finished evaluating, so it also sits above every mod hook and can time the total. Mod overhead = outer - inner.

REMOTE   Press 0 three times within 1.5s to toggle the cluster. LEFT/RIGHT tab. UP/DOWN scroll. OK emits a report. BACK closes. (YELLOW is NOT used: YouTube's own leanback UI claims it, and screensaver-fix.js synthesises a YELLOW press every 30s on Shorts.) CONSOLE  __PERF.help(), __PERF.toggle()

Comments panel fix - https://github.com/NicholasBly/youtube-webos/issues/188

Bug (YouTube-side, also happens on the stock app, started late Sept 2026): pressing Back on the comments panel adds a "closing" class to <ytlr-animated-overlay> (currently `frHKed`). YouTube's CSS for that class collapses the panel contents to 0x0 immediately, but the comment list stays mounted for ~350ms while the close animation runs. The list watches its rows with a ResizeObserver, so it records every row as 0 tall and saves that into the per-video list state. Reopening restores that state: all rows stack at the top with height 0 and arrow-key navigation gets stuck.

The same thing happens to the Description panel, which uses the same overlay.

Fix: for every YouTube CSS rule tied to the closing classes that hides or zero-sizes something, add an override that keeps the element laid out but invisible. The panel looks the same while it closes, the ResizeObserver never sees 0, and the saved state keeps the real heights.

The closing class is ALSO briefly present while a panel opens, and the Description panel's rows are built and measured during that moment - so the override has to be in place before the first panel ever opens. The rules are found by scanning the stylesheets at startup (every second while the set of stylesheets still changes, for at most STARTUP_MAX_TRIES), with a scan on panel focus as a backstop. A broad fallback is used until the real rule is found.

The closing classes, the overlay and the panel are in core/selectors.js (PANEL_CLOSING_CLASSES, ANIMATED_OVERLAY, OVERLAY_PANEL).

Caps MSE SourceBuffer memory by evicting already-played data.

The YouTube TV player leaves a large read-behind window in the SourceBuffer. On webOS 3/4 hardware (Chromium 38/53, ~1GB total RAM) that window plus the read-ahead can push the web process past what LG's memory manager tolerates, which kills the app with the "restarting to free memory" toast.

Chromium only garbage-collects a SourceBuffer once it hits its own internal ceiling (150MB video / 12MB audio on these builds). The trim keeps well below that.

Legacy webOS (Chromium 38 / webOS 3) polyfills.

This file replaces core-js. core-js's compat data considers Chromium 38 to need 386 modules (~334 KiB of source) because it re-implements any built-in with *any* spec deviation - Promise, Map, Set, Symbol, URL and most of Array.prototype included. None of those deviations affect this app, and `usage-pure` mode also rewrites every `arr.slice(...)` call site into `_sliceInstanceProperty(arr).call(arr, ...)`, which costs a function call and a property lookup on every invocation, forever, on every device.

So we ship only what Chromium 38 genuinely does not have and this codebase genuinely calls, with one deliberate exception: iteration over DOM collections (dom.js), kept as a guard. Everything is feature-detected: on webOS 4 (Chromium 53) Object.entries, Object.values and Node#isConnected are still installed, on webOS 5 and 6 nothing is.

The comment on each entry is the first Chrome version shipping it. tests/unit/polyfill-conformance-test.cjs differentially tests every one of these against the platform-native implementation.

If you use a newer built-in in src/, add it to the matching group: define.js            the non-enumerable installer the groups share dom.js               Element#closest, Node#isConnected, iterable collections object.js            Object.assign, entries, values array.js             Array.from, find, findIndex string.js            startsWith url-search-params.js URLSearchParams and url.searchParams

What counts: every category the user has not switched off. Auto Skip and Manual Skip segments come off because they will be skipped past; Show in Seek Bar segments come off too, which is what was asked for. Disable means the segment plays in full, so it stays in the running time.

Why the merge: SponsorBlock regularly returns overlapping segments for the same stretch of video - a sponsor read that is also tagged self-promo, for instance - and summing the raw durations would subtract that stretch twice and report a video shorter than it can possibly be.

functions.name: pickFullLabel
functions.description: The category to show for a video that is entirely one category (sponsor first, by FULL_PRIORITY), leaving out categories set to Disable; null when there is none.

functions.name: buildCss
functions.description: Build the rules for the current state. Empty string means "show nothing".

functions.name: SponsorBlockLabels.constructor
functions.description: No <style> element until there is something to write.

functions.name: SponsorBlockLabels.write
functions.description: Puts `css` in the labels' <style> element (creating it when needed); unchanged CSS is not written again.

functions.name: SponsorBlockLabels.update
functions.description: Recomputes both readouts (the handler's updateLabels says when).

functions.name: SponsorBlockLabels.clear
functions.description: Removes every label.

functions.name: enterMutedSegment
functions.description: Mutes for `seg`, remembering the state to restore; a no-op while already muted for it.

functions.name: leaveMutedSegment
functions.description: Restores the mute state unless `time` is still inside the muted segment; without a time (or with NaN) it always restores.

functions.name: anchorOf
functions.description: The element the overlay sits beside for `bar`: YouTube's progress-bar renderer around it, else ytlr-progress-bar, else the bar itself.

functions.name: getProgressBarAnchor
functions.description: The anchor of the tracked bar (anchorOf). The overlay is always a sibling of it, because YouTube's renderer destroys foreign children. Null while there is no bar, or the bar has no parent to be a sibling in.

functions.name: forgetAnchor
functions.description: Forgets the cached anchor; the next getProgressBarAnchor() recomputes it.

functions.name: offsetRelativeTo
functions.description: The offset of `el` within `ancestor`, so the sibling overlay can be placed over exactly the same box.

functions.name: syncOverlayPosition
functions.description: Puts the overlay over the tracked bar's box, at its visibility.

functions.name: resyncOverlay
functions.description: Re-syncs the overlay with the tracked bar now; nothing to do without either.

functions.name: resyncOverlayThrottled
functions.description: resyncOverlay at most every OVERLAY_SYNC_MS: the timeupdate path, which fires at about 4 Hz while the viewport rarely changes.

functions.name: drawOverlay
functions.description: Draws (or keeps) the overlay for the current segments and settings beside the tracked bar. False when the bar is gone from the document: the caller then looks for it again. True otherwise, including when nothing needs drawing.

functions.name: recolourOverlay
functions.description: Gives every mark its category's colour as the settings have it now: a colour picked in the panel (one change per step of a drag) repaints the marks rather than rebuilding the overlay.

functions.name: SponsorBlockUI.constructor
functions.description: Hidden, with no segments; the popup element is built the first time it is shown.

functions.name: SponsorBlockUI.createPopup
functions.description: Builds the popup (header and an empty list) and adds it to the page, once.

functions.name: SponsorBlockUI.updateSegments
functions.description: Remembers the list; the rows are built when the popup is shown, not per video.

functions.name: SponsorBlockUI.renderRows
functions.description: Rebuilds the list: one row per segment with its colour, label and time, then shows the popup.

functions.name: SponsorBlockUI.togglePopup
functions.description: Shows or hides the popup (the options panel shows it beside the SponsorBlock page); shown only while the video has segments.

functions.name: categoryName
functions.description: The category's name inside a sentence.

functions.name: skipMessage
functions.description: The toast after a skip, for the names of the categories skipped (repeats dropped): "Skipped sponsored segment", "Skipped intro and sponsored segment", "Skipped a, b, and c segment".

functions.name: categoryLabel
functions.description: The category's label in a list.

functions.name: rebuildSkipSegments
functions.description: Rebuilds `sb.skipSegments` from the API's segments and the settings: the segments to act on, in start order, each with its mode (auto_skip, manual_skip or mute) and its index in `sb.segments`.

functions.name: findSegmentAtTime
functions.description: Index of the segment `time` is in, or -1. Segments overlap (a self-promo inside a sponsor, say), so this is a scan rather than a binary search, and when several contain the time a manual one wins over an auto-skip one, which wins over a muted one: a skip must stop at a manual segment, and a skip takes a muted part with it.

functions.name: findNextSegmentIndex
functions.description: Index of the first segment starting at or after `time` (binary search on the sorted starts).

functions.name: clampSegments
functions.description: Clamps the segments to the video's duration, and short of it on the legacy engines; true when anything moved, so the caller rebuilds the skip list. The end always comes from the one the API gave (`apiEnd`, kept on the first clamp), so a short duration reported first and the real one later give the segment back its end.

functions.name: attachTimeListener
functions.description: Starts listening to timeupdate on a playing video (once).

functions.name: detachTimeListener
functions.description: Stops listening to timeupdate.

functions.name: startHighFreqLoop
functions.description: Starts the per-frame check when a segment is coming up, so the skip lands on time rather than up to a timeupdate (about 250 ms) late.

functions.name: stopHighFreqLoop
functions.description: Stops the per-frame check.

functions.name: highFreqLoop
functions.description: One frame of the check: hands over to handleTimeUpdate once the playhead reaches the next segment, else asks for the next frame. Stops on pause, a skip or destroy.

functions.name: aimAt
functions.description: Aims at the segment containing `time`, else the first one after it.

functions.name: aimPast
functions.description: Aims past `time`, and stops listening when nothing is left.

functions.name: resetSegmentTracking
functions.description: Re-aims from the playhead and re-arms the listener: after a seek, when playback resumes and after the skip list changed. The manual-skip prompt stays up while the playhead is still inside its segment, so resuming there does not blink it off and on.

functions.name: refreshSkipSegments
functions.description: Rebuilds the skip list for the current settings and re-aims.

functions.name: clearManualNotification
functions.description: Removes the manual-skip prompt and forgets the segment it offered.

functions.name: armSkipWatchdog
functions.description: Safety net: if the media pipeline swallows the 'seeked' event for a programmatic skip (buffer stalls / near-EOS quirks on webOS), clear the isSkipping latch so the timeupdate pipeline keeps working.

functions.name: clearSkipWatchdog
functions.description: Stops the timer that catches a skip whose seek never completed.

functions.name: findCurrentSegment
functions.description: Index of the segment `currentTime` is in. The predicted one is trusted when it is a manual segment; otherwise the scan decides, since a manual segment nested in the predicted one takes precedence (see findSegmentAtTime).

functions.name: announceSegment
functions.description: The manual-skip prompt for a segment that is not auto-skipped.

functions.name: shouldSkip
functions.description: Whether an auto-skip segment is skipped now, or left alone.

functions.name: findJumpTarget
functions.description: Where the skip lands: past this segment and the auto-skip segments that follow it closely, but never past the start of a manual one ahead of the playhead. A manual segment already behind the playhead has had its turn, and a muted segment is skipped over like any other part of the video.

functions.name: skipTo
functions.params: sb, segmentIdx, currentTime, { jumpTarget, categories, indices }
functions.description: Performs the skip, then aims at whatever follows the landing point.

functions.name: skipAutoSegment
functions.description: The auto-skip segment at `segmentIdx`, with the ones close behind it, in one jump; unless shouldSkip leaves it alone. The timeupdate path and the chain at the start (chain.js) both come here.

functions.name: handleTimeUpdate
functions.description: The skip decision at the playhead: leaves a muted segment, polls faster before the next segment, and inside one auto-skips, mutes, or offers the manual skip according to its category's mode.

functions.name: bindWindowEvents
functions.description: Called once, when the segments arrive; undone by the handler's bag.

functions.name: bindVideoEvents
functions.description: Called from bindVideo(); undone by the per-video bag.

functions.name: bindVideoEvents.listen
functions.description: A listener on the bound <video> that goes with the per-video bag.

functions.name: capSet
functions.description: Sets `key`, dropping the oldest entry at `limit`; returns the dropped key, or null.

functions.name: capMarker
functions.description: What CACHE_CAP_KEY holds: the ladder's rung and the cache revision, e.g. "3r2".

functions.name: dropStoredCache
functions.description: Forgets the stored answers and records the ladder the next ones are measured against.

functions.name: loadCache
functions.description: Loads the known best thumbnail of each video from localStorage ("id:rank" pairs); a cache written for another strategy or an older revision is dropped instead.

functions.name: saveCache
functions.description: Writes the confirmed entries of the cache, with the strategy marker they are valid for.

functions.name: scheduleSave
functions.description: Saves the cache after CACHE_SAVE_DEBOUNCE ms, once for a burst of new answers.

functions.name: cancelSave
functions.description: Drops a pending save: for a cache that is about to be cleared anyway.

functions.name: flushCache
functions.description: Saves a pending change now (the app is going to the background).

functions.name: upgradeItem
functions.description: Upgrades the thumbnails of one item of a list (a tile with its long-press menu copy, or the other renderer kinds); returns how many URLs it changed.

functions.name: upgradeItems
functions.description: upgradeItem over a list; returns the total changed.

functions.name: upgradeListInto
functions.description: One shelf list upgraded, its changes added to `tally` (forEachItemList's argument).

functions.name: upgradeSectionList
functions.description: The shelves of a section list. The list itself does not count as found (state.listsSeen): a list whose shelves the walk does not know holds no item list it can reach, and is scanned.

functions.name: isThumbnailFreeContinuation
functions.description: Whether every key of the continuation is one known to hold no thumbnails.

functions.name: upgradeAutoplaySets
functions.description: Upgrades the next-video item of each autoplay set.

functions.name: upgradeAutoplay
functions.description: Upgrades the autoplay suggestions of a watch response: the sets, the modified sets and the replay card.

functions.name: upgradeBrowseTabs
functions.description: Upgrades the sections of every tab of a browse page's secondary navigation.

functions.name: upgradeActions
functions.description: Upgrades the items that reload or append actions (continuations) carry.

functions.name: upgradeContinuation
functions.description:
Continuation payloads, in all four shapes.

Called for every response rather than only for responseType 'CONTINUATION', because a continuation is not always classified as one. A shelf continuation under the playing video arrives with `contents.singleColumnWatchNextResults` still attached, and detectResponseType() checks NEXT before CONTINUATION — so the response is typed NEXT while every thumbnail in it lives under `continuationContents.sectionListContinuation`.

functions.name: scanForThumbnails
functions.description: Last-resort bounded walk, used only when the schema paths produced nothing. Keeps the module working through an InnerTube reshuffle instead of silently doing nothing, without ever putting a full traversal on the hot path.

functions.name: scanRoot
functions.description: Where the thumbnail scan of a response type starts: down SCAN_FROM's path as far as it exists.

functions.name: upgradeByType
functions.description: The thumbnails at the known paths of `type`, rewritten; the count. A type whose paths reach no item list at all gets the bounded scan, an unknown type gets it when the body is large enough to be worth one, and a type with nothing to find gets neither.

functions.name: upgradeResponseThumbnails
functions.description: Entry point called from the JSON.parse hook in adblock/parse-hook.js. `responseType` is the type adblock already detected, so this costs no extra detection pass; `textLength` is the length of the JSON text, which the hook already has.

functions.name: handleVisibilityChange
functions.description: Saves the cache when the app goes to the background; back in the foreground, holds the probes off for a moment.

functions.name: cleanup
functions.description: Stops everything in flight; `keepCache` false drops the pending save instead of writing it.

functions.name: resetVerification
functions.description: Forget every verified rank. The cache is only meaningful against the ladder that produced it: 'sd' records sddefault as a video's answer, the other modes record maxres or the floor. A cached answer is never re-probed, so crossing that line would freeze every known video at the old mode's ceiling. Starting over costs one re-probe per video, spread over normal use.

functions.name: usefulRankFor
functions.description: The best rung the current mode will emit or probe for. A single rung, deliberately: maxresdefault and hq720 are both 1280x720 for the overwhelming majority of uploads, so probing a second rung doubled verification traffic to distinguish two files of identical size. A miss falls straight to the guaranteed floor. In 'sd' mode the rung is sddefault instead.

functions.name: drawsUnproven
functions.description: Whether the mode draws its rung before any proof and corrects a miss afterwards ('sd' and 'eager'), or draws only what is known to exist and waits for the probe ('safe'). sddefault exists for nearly every video and maxres for most, so a miss is rare; waiting showed every new tile at the rung YouTube listed (hqdefault) and swapped it a few hundred ms later.

functions.name: rankOf
functions.description: The rank of a thumbnail basename; undefined for a name the ladder cannot map.

functions.name: buildUrl
functions.description: The `/vi/` JPEG URL of one rung; hqdefault.jpg exists for every video.

functions.name: onNavKey
functions.description: Arrow keydown, capture phase: just a timestamp, nothing else runs here.

functions.name: navPauseLeft
functions.description: Milliseconds left on the navigation pause; 0 when the remote is quiet.

functions.name: headExists
functions.description: Whether the URL exists, by a HEAD request: true, false, UNKNOWN, or null when the answer carried no readable Content-Length (a cross-origin answer on Chromium 38 and 53), in which case the caller loads the image instead. A grey placeholder answered 200 with a tiny body counts as missing too.

functions.name: headExists.xhr.onload
functions.description: A 2xx answer: whether the file is bigger than YouTube's grey placeholder (null when the size is not given); anything else is missing.

functions.name: headExists.xhr.onerror
functions.description: A network error: unknown.

functions.name: headExists.xhr.ontimeout
functions.description: A timeout: unknown.

functions.name: imageExists
functions.description: Whether the URL exists, by loading the image. Used for tiles the app has already rendered. In the modes that draw unproven rungs the tile shows this very URL, so the load comes out of the browser's cache, whatever made the tile grey included (a missing rung loads as the grey placeholder, caught on its width below); in the mode that waits for proof the tile shows the floor, and the image loaded here is the one the promotion then draws, so the download is not wasted. It also needs no CORS at all, and a CSS background-image load never passes through fetch or XMLHttpRequest, so the is the only place this signal exists. An `error` is a load that never got an answer, not a miss.

functions.name: imageExists.finish
functions.description: Settles the probe once, with its timer and the image's handlers cleared.

functions.name: imageExists.img.onload
functions.description: A missing derivative can also come back 200 with a grey placeholder, which loads fine and has to be caught on its dimensions instead.

functions.name: imageExists.img.onerror
functions.description: The image failed to load: unknown (a 404 and a network error look the same to an ).

functions.name: resolveQuality
functions.description: The mode's best rung if it exists, else the guaranteed floor. On screen the image is asked (imageExists: cached in Fast mode, the promotion's own load otherwise); off screen a HEAD, because an there would pull down a full image nobody is looking at.

functions.name: clearProbeTiers
functions.description: Forgets the latest parse and its budget; part of the module's cleanup.

functions.name: scheduleProbe
functions.description: Queues a probe of `videoId`'s thumbnail sizes, unless its answer is cached, it was tried this session, or the session's probe limit is reached.

functions.name: applyCorrection
functions.description: Rewrites the entries we gambled on now that the answer is known; true when there were entries to write to. An entry already drawn at that rung stays as it is: its URL may be a signed or vi_webp form of the same file, and the /vi/ JPEG a new download.

functions.name: settledRank
functions.description: Resolved rank clamped to what the video was already known to support.

functions.name: onProbeDone
functions.description: A probe's answer: counts it, drops it when the strategy changed meanwhile, saves a real answer to the cache, corrects the tiles on screen, and starts the next probe.

functions.name: deferProbes
functions.description: Called from the parse. The first videos this parse queued are the top of the response - what the user is looking at - so a small burst of them goes through immediately; everything else waits for the surface to settle.

functions.name: takeFrom
functions.description: Appends to `picked`, up to `limit`, the ids of `set` that are queued (or all of them when `inQueue` is false).

functions.name: pickProbeIds
functions.description: Up to `limit` queued ids: the on-screen ones first, then the latest parse's in the order it queued them, then the head of the queue. Each tier is read from its own small set against the queue, so a drain costs the size of those sets plus `limit`, not a pass over the whole queue (up to PROBE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT ids, drained three at a time).

functions.name: admitToTier
functions.description: Whether a picked video may go now, spending the budget of its tier.

functions.name: startProbe
functions.description: Starts the probe of one video, unless the cache has the answer already.

functions.name: runProbeRound
functions.description: One round of the queue, from the idle callback: as many probes as the slots and tiers allow.

functions.name: drainProbes
functions.description: Starts the probe pump in idle time, or waits while the remote is moving through rows.

functions.name: schedulePromotionSweep
functions.description: The one sweep timer: a sweep already pending keeps its time.

functions.name: runPromotionSweep
functions.description: Only runs when verification disagrees with what was already emitted, which after the first session is rare. Batched into one sweep so N corrections cost one querySelectorAll, not N.

functions.name: renderedThumbnails
functions.description: Calls `fn(element, videoId, backgroundImage)` for every rendered tile whose background is a thumbnail. No try: the selector is a constant, and a try would keep this loop (every sample and every sweep) unoptimised on webOS 3.

functions.name: sampleRenderedIds
functions.description: The videoIds on screen, sampled at most once per VISIBLE_SAMPLE_TTL.

functions.name: sameIds
functions.description: Whether two sets hold the same ids.

functions.name: upgradeVideo
functions.description:
Rewrites the matched entries `from` to `to` (triples, all of one video) to the rung the mode may emit, and returns how many URLs changed. What the video may get is decided once for all of them: a container holds one video, usually more than once (the tile header and its long-press menu).

The emitted rung is the useful one (sddefault in 'sd', else maxres). A cached probe answer clamps it; for a video not probed yet the modes that draw unproven rungs ('sd', 'eager') emit it as it is, and 'safe' clamps it to `proven`, the best rung shipped in this response, with the better one landing on a later parse. Either way a probe is scheduled when the useful rung is unproven. Entry width/height are left alone; the app sizes tiles from them.

functions.name: pendingEntriesOf
functions.description: The entries of a video we gambled on, for the write-back (each followed by the rung it is drawn at), with what the video is already known to support recorded beside them; the list is capped so a long session cannot grow it without bound. Eviction is safe: it only costs that video the write-back, and the DOM sweep still covers it.

functions.name: upgradeContainer
functions.description: Rewrite every URL in a thumbnail container in place. Handles both `{ thumbnails: [...] }` (tileRenderer and friends) and `{ sources: [...] }` (the newer *ViewModel schema).

functions.name: clearStateTimer
functions.description: Clears the timer in `state[name]`, if one is set.

functions.name: destroyVideoQuality
functions.description: Leaves the player: timers, listeners and the per-video state go (the webOS 25 kick stays done for the session).

functions.name: attachToPlayer
functions.description: Attaches to the TV player once it is there; true when attached (pollUntil's answer).

functions.name: pollForPlayer
functions.description: Looks for the player every 200 ms for the first ten seconds, then once a second for another fifty: a slow first load must still be forced, and a watch page whose player never mounts is not polled for the rest of the session. The poll is cancelled with the bag, so a detached module is never looked for.

functions.name: initVideoQuality
functions.description: Attaches to the player on the watch page (polling until it exists) and sets the stored quality preference.

functions.name: handleNavigation
functions.description: Attaches on entering the watch page (a tick later, once the page is built) and detaches on leaving it.

functions.name: setupListeners
functions.description: Follows page changes, and checks the current page once the document is ready.

functions.name: ensurePlaybackStarts
functions.description: Nothing to kick on webOS 3 to 6.

functions.name: dismissRaisedControls
functions.description: The kick raises the controls bar: when it holds the focus it is hidden (ui/hide-controls.js) and dismissed with three UP presses. All of it is the attach's (`bag`), so leaving the watch page cancels what has not run.

functions.name: ensurePlaybackStarts
functions.description: webOS 25 only, once per session: calls playVideo() until the player reports PLAYING (up to KICKSTART_MAX_ATTEMPTS), then hides the controls that raised with it.

functions.name: handleStateChange
functions.description: The player's state change: published as yt-player-state-change for the clock and SponsorBlock, then, with Force Max Quality on, the quality is forced for a new video.

functions.name: isPlayerQualityKnown
functions.description: True once the player reports any negotiated quality (see KNOWN_QUALITIES).

functions.name: isForcedPair
functions.description: The 4320/4320 pair this module writes: the app's own preference is any other.

functions.name: pairOf
functions.description: The quality pair inside a stored record (its `data` is a JSON string), or null.

functions.name: setLocalStorageQuality
functions.description: Stores the 4320 pair, unless ours is there with more than RENEW_BEFORE_MS left. Read every time: the app stores its own pair whenever the viewer picks a quality.

functions.name: clearLocalStorageQuality
functions.description: The setting turned off: removes the 4320 preference written above, so the app chooses the quality itself again. A preference of any other shape is the app's own and stays.

functions.name: setQualityOnPlayer
functions.description: Asks the player for the highest quality, unless it already plays at it; says whether that was an upgrade and to what.

functions.name: notifyIfUpgraded
functions.description: Toasts the new quality half a second after an upgrade (dropped when the watch page was left meanwhile).

functions.name: settleVideo
functions.description: Marks the video settled when the player already reports a quality; else runs `force(videoId)`.

functions.name: interceptAndUpgradeQuality
functions.description: A video already playing without a quality: pause, force, resume.

functions.name: isForceEnabled
functions.description: Whether quality is forced now: Force Max Quality is on and the player is not an inline preview.

functions.name: createTimeFormatter
functions.description: Hours and minutes in the TV's language. Intl is in Chrome 24+, so webOS 3 has it; a language tag Intl refuses (a POSIX suffix such as "en-US@posix") would throw and leave no clock at all, so it falls back to the default locale.

functions.name: listItems
functions.description: The comma-separated items of a computed transition longhand; parentheses keep their commas.

functions.name: readPlayerFade
functions.description: YouTube's own fade for its player UI: the first opacity (or all) transition on the controls, the player shadow, or an ancestor of either up to the player shell. '' when none of them has one (or they are not rendered yet).

functions.name: Watch.constructor
functions.description: The clock: builds the element, starts the minute ticks and the listeners, and adds it to the page.

functions.name: Watch.createClock
functions.description: The clock element; its look comes from watch.css and the theme classes on <html>.

functions.name: Watch.startClock
functions.description: Shows the time now and at the start of every minute, and again when the app returns to the foreground.

functions.name: Watch.startClock.setTime
functions.description: Its timer and listener go with the bag, before the element: no tick runs after destroy().

functions.name: Watch.startClock.tick
functions.description: Shows the time, then aims the next tick at the next whole minute.

functions.name: Watch.observePlayer
functions.description: Watches `player`'s focus attribute (null: none), reading the fade again for a new one.

functions.name: Watch.onPlayerToggle
functions.description: YouTube showed or hid its player UI: follow it now, with its fade.

functions.name: Watch.isOverlayOpen
functions.description: Whether a side panel (description, comments, save) is open over the player.

functions.name: Watch.setHidden
functions.description: Hides or shows the clock (a class, so the fade applies).

functions.name: Watch.updateVisibility
functions.description: Decides the visibility from scratch: shown off the watch page; on it, hidden while the video alone is showing, the player or nothing holds the focus, or a side panel is open.

functions.name: Watch.setupGlobalListeners
functions.description: Re-decides the visibility (debounced) on play, pause and a new video, on every focus change, and on a page change (with the cached elements dropped).

functions.name: Watch.destroy
functions.description: Removes the clock, its timer and its listeners.

functions.name: toggleWatch
functions.description: Creates or destroys the clock to match Display Time in UI.

functions.name: currentTimeFor
functions.description: Find the currentTime of the <video> driving this MediaSource.

functions.name: trimSourceBuffer
functions.description: Removes what lies more than RETAIN_BEHIND_SECS behind the playhead from one SourceBuffer, unless it is busy or the slice is too small to bother.

functions.name: patchAppend
functions.description: Patches appendBuffer on the SourceBuffer prototype (once), so an append that arrives while a trim is running waits for it instead of throwing.

functions.name: patchAppend.proto.appendBuffer
functions.description: appendBuffer that defers itself to the trim's updateend when a trim is in progress.

functions.name: patchAppend.proto.appendBuffer.onDone
functions.description: Runs the deferred append once the trim has finished.

functions.name: tick
functions.description: Every TRIM_INTERVAL_MS: trims the buffers of every open MediaSource and forgets the closed ones.

functions.name: bufferStats
functions.description: On-device verification, with diagnostics on (localStorage ytaf-debug=1 and a reload): run __ytafBufferStats() in the console while a video plays. `behind` should hold near RETAIN_BEHIND_SECS instead of climbing with playback position.

functions.name: installBufferLimit
functions.description: Installs the buffer cap: tracks MediaSources as the player creates them, remembers their blob URLs, and starts the trim timer.

functions.name: installBufferLimit.MediaSource.prototype.addSourceBuffer
functions.description: addSourceBuffer that also tracks the MediaSource and patches the new buffer's appends.

functions.name: installBufferLimit.URL.createObjectURL
functions.description: createObjectURL that remembers a MediaSource's blob URL, which is how currentTimeFor() finds its <video>.

functions.name: callListener
functions.description: Runs one listener; one that throws is logged and the rest still run, as on an event target.

functions.name: FetchRegistry.constructor
functions.description: Wraps window.fetch; private, as there is one registry (getInstance()).

functions.name: FetchRegistry.getInstance
functions.description: The one registry, created (and fetch wrapped) on first use.

functions.name: FetchRegistry.addEventListener
functions.description: Adds a listener for `type` ('request'); it can cancel a request with preventDefault().

functions.name: FetchRegistry.removeEventListener
functions.description: Removes a listener added with addEventListener.

functions.name: FetchRegistry.#dispatch
functions.description: Calls the listeners with a cancelable event; false when one prevented it.

functions.name: FetchRegistry.#customFetch
functions.description: Not async: on the fast path the original promise is returned as is, with no wrapper promise, no URL object and no event. The registry exists once Tracking Block was first turned on (features/adblock/tracking-block.js); turned off again it has no listener, and every request takes this path. The cast block (features/block-webos-cast) does its own check without it.

functions.name: FetchRegistry.#hookedFetch
functions.description: The slow path: numbers and logs the request when diagnostics are on, lets the 'request' listeners see and cancel it (a cancelled one fails like a network error), then fetches.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.resolveCommand
functions.description: YouTube's resolveCommand, as replaced: the first hook whose key the command has handles it; any other command goes to the original.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.constructor
functions.description: Replaces resolveCommand on the instance found under window._yttv[hookTargetName], keeping the original bound.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.checkHookTarget
functions.description: Whether window._yttv[targetName] is the object that owns resolveCommand.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.findHookTarget

functions.description: That key, waiting for YouTube to create it: polled with a doubling delay until POLL_TIMEOUT_MS.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.getHookTarget.poll
functions.description: One look for the key; schedules the next with a doubled delay, or rejects past the deadline.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.getInstance
functions.description: The registry, once YouTube's resolveCommand exists; concurrent callers share one wait, and a timed-out wait is retried by the next call.

functions.name: ResolveCommandRegistry.setHook

functions.name: main
functions.description: Opens YouTube with the launch parameters webOS started the app with.

functions.name: def
functions.description: Non-enumerable install, matching how the engine defines built-ins. A plain assignment on a prototype would make the method visible to for-in loops over arrays/strings and could break unrelated YouTube code.

functions.name: Element.prototype.closest
functions.description: Element.closest for engines without it (Chromium 38).

functions.name: serialise
functions.description: Encodes a name or value as application/x-www-form-urlencoded (spaces as +).

functions.name: deserialise
functions.description: Decodes a name or value (+ as a space); a malformed escape keeps its raw text, as browsers do.

functions.name: USP
functions.description: URLSearchParams for Chromium 38: from a query string, another instance, an array of pairs or an object.

functions.name: USP.prototype._changed
functions.description: Tells the URL this instance belongs to (url.searchParams) that the parameters changed.

functions.name: USP.prototype.append
functions.description: Adds a pair, after the existing ones.

functions.name: USP.prototype.getAll
functions.description: Every value of `name`, in order.

functions.name: USP.prototype.has
functions.description: Whether `name` is present.

functions.name: USP.prototype.get
functions.description: The first value of `name`, or null.

functions.name: USP.prototype.set
functions.description: Spec: replace the first occurrence in place, drop the rest.

functions.name: USP.prototype['delete']
functions.description: Removes every pair named `name`.

functions.name: USP.prototype.sort
functions.description: Spec: by name in UTF-16 code units, equal names kept in their order. Chromium 38's sort is not stable, so the position breaks the ties.

functions.name: pairIterator
functions.description: An iterator over the pairs, live as the native one, giving `pick(name, value)`.

functions.name: pairIterator.iterator.next
functions.description: The next pair, as `pick` shapes it, or done.

functions.name: pairIterator.iterator[Symbol.iterator]
functions.description: The iterator is its own iterable (for...of).

functions.name: USP.prototype.keys
functions.description: An iterator of the names.

functions.name: USP.prototype.values
functions.description: An iterator of the values.

functions.name: USP.prototype.entries
functions.description: An iterator of [name, value] pairs.

functions.name: USP.prototype.forEach
functions.description: Calls `cb(value, name, params)` for every pair, in order.

functions.name: USP.prototype.toString
functions.description: The parameters as a query string, without the leading ?.

functions.name: urlLacksSearchParams
functions.description: Whether `new URL()` lacks url.searchParams: Chromium 38 has URL without it (Chrome 51).

functions.name: wireURLSearchParams
functions.description: url.searchParams over `SearchParams`, wired to url.search in both directions: a change of the params writes url.search, and url.search written since the last read (or href) gives the same object the new query.

functions.name: wireURLSearchParams.sp._onChange
functions.description: Writes a change of url.searchParams back into the URL's search.

functions.name: createElement
functions.description: Builds an element: `props` sets attributes and properties, with `class`, `text`, `style` (an object) and `events` (type to listener) handled specially; strings among `children` become text nodes.

functions.name: showControls
functions.description: Lifts the hiding now; a no-op when nothing is hidden.

functions.name: hideControlsFor
functions.description: Hides them for `ms` (a second call extends the window); returns showControls.

functions.name: createConfigCheckbox
functions.description: A checkbox row for boolean setting `key`, labelled with its description; it writes the setting when toggled and follows changes made elsewhere.

functions.name: setUnavailable
functions.description: Greys a row out and drops it from the focus order, or restores it: the setting it carries does nothing right now (Tracking Block without Ad Blocking, the thumbnail strategy without the upgrade). Greyed out and kept in place rather than hidden, so the user sees why and the rows below do not jump.

functions.name: createColorPicker
functions.description: A colour input and an R (reset to default) button for colour setting `colorKey`; it follows changes made elsewhere.

functions.name: createControlRow
functions.description: A focusable row: the label on the left, `< value >` on the right. Left and Right (and a click on the row) step the value; the arrows are clickable too. Enter is the panel's: its keyboard handler clicks the focused row. Returns the row and the function that refreshes its value.

functions.name: createControlRow.updateDisplay
functions.description: Shows the current value.

functions.name: createControlRow.unavailable
functions.description: Whether the row is greyed out (setUnavailable): a greyed-out row steps nothing, by key or by pointer.

functions.name: createControlRow.onLeft
functions.description: Steps the value back, unless the row is greyed out.

functions.name: createControlRow.onRight
functions.description: Steps the value forward, unless the row is greyed out.

functions.name: createControlRow.arrow
functions.description: A clickable < or > arrow for the pointer (Magic Remote).

functions.name: createCycleControl
functions.description: A row that cycles `configKey` through `modes`; `displayMap` turns a mode into its label.

functions.name: createCycleControl.displayValue
functions.description: The label of the setting's current value (the value itself when the map has none).

functions.name: createCycleControl.cycle
functions.description: Writes the next (step 1) or previous (-1) value in `modes`, wrapping around.

functions.name: createAlignedCycleControl
functions.description: A cycle row that sits among checkbox rows. Its label is indented by one checkbox (the ytaf-aligned rule in controls.css) and starts with the same no-break space the checkbox labels use, so the text lines up with them.

functions.name: createLogoControl
functions.description: The YouTube Logo row (Default, Premium, Hidden).

functions.name: createVideoCodecControl
functions.description: The Force Video Codec row.

functions.name: createThemeControl
functions.description: The UI Theme row.

functions.name: createThumbnailQualityControl
functions.description: The Thumbnail Strategy row, greyed out while Max Thumbnail Quality is off.

functions.name: createThumbnailQualityControl.sync
functions.description: The strategy only means anything while the feature it tunes is on.

functions.name: createSegmentControl
functions.description: The row of one SponsorBlock category (`sbMode_<category>`): its modes, with the category's colour picker.

functions.name: createShortcutControl
functions.description: The row of one shortcut key (0-9, red, green, blue): the action it runs.

functions.name: createPreviewControl
functions.description: The Force Previews row (Disabled, Force On, Force Off).

functions.name: createOpacityControl
functions.description: A 0-100 % row in steps of 5 for setting `key` (the video shelf opacity), greyed out while OLED-Care Mode is off.

functions.name: createOpacityControl.changeValue
functions.description: Adds `delta` to the stored value, kept within 0-100.

functions.name: createOpacityControl.sync
functions.description: The shelf opacity applies under OLED-Care Mode only (ui/styles/html-classes.js).

functions.name: createSection
functions.description: A titled group of rows; `variant` adds a class (ytaf-section-2col lays the rows out in two columns).

functions.name: createFocusTrap
functions.description: `container` is the panel element, `allowed(target)` says whether a focus outside the container is fine anyway (the SponsorBlock popup), `firstControl()` is where focus goes when the last safe place is gone.

functions.name: createFocusTrap.onFocus
functions.description: Capture-phase focus listener: a focus outside the panel (and outside the allowed popup) is sent back to the last place inside.

functions.name: createFocusTrap.attach
functions.description: Starts trapping, with `initial` as the place focus is sent back to.

functions.name: createFocusTrap.detach
functions.description: Stops trapping.

functions.name: swallowUntilReleased
functions.description: Swallows the key that closed the panel until it is released: a held Back repeats, and the repeats would otherwise reach YouTube (a page back) once the panel's handler is gone.

functions.name: swallowUntilReleased.onDown
functions.description: Eats the held key's repeats.

functions.name: swallowUntilReleased.release
functions.description: Stops swallowing: both listeners and the 2 s safety timer go.

functions.name: swallowUntilReleased.onUp
functions.description: The key was released: stop swallowing it.

functions.name: pageFocusables
functions.description: The controls of `page` that can take focus, in document order.

functions.name: boxOf
functions.description: The box a move measures: a checkbox's whole label row, not the small box at its left, which would overlap nothing above or below it.

functions.name: nearestInDirection
functions.description: The candidate nearest to `from` in `dir`, judged by the centres of their boxes (boxOf). Left and Right stay within the row: only candidates that overlap `from` vertically count. Up and Down prefer a candidate that overlaps `from` horizontally but take the nearest one otherwise. Among those, the one closest ahead wins, then the one closest sideways. Returns null when nothing lies that way.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard
functions.description: @param {HTMLElement} elContainer the panel element @param {object} ctx  `tabBtns` (the tab buttons), `activePage` (live index), `pages()` (the four page elements, unbuilt ones undefined), `close()` @returns {{ attach(): void, detach(): void }} the key handler, to be put on the document while the panel is open

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.markLabel
functions.description: Chrome 38 to 59 have no :focus-within, so the label row of the focused control carries a class instead (panel.css).

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.focusables
functions.description: The tab buttons and the controls of the open page, in document order.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.moveFocus
functions.description: Moves the focus to the nearest focusable control in direction `dir`.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.moveHorizontal
functions.description: Left and Right: within the row, and around the ends of the tab bar.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.moveVertical
functions.description: Up and Down: between the open tab and its page, wrapping at both ends.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.onPointerMove
functions.description: The pointer moved: OK presses are the pointer's from now on.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.onCursorState
functions.description: webOS showed or hid the pointer (it hides it after a while, or on an arrow key).

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.onClick
functions.description: Drops a pointer click that comes with the Enter press that already clicked.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.onKeyUp
functions.description: Enter released: a click it brings can still follow, briefly.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.clickFocused
functions.description: Clicks the focused control, as the Enter key; the click this sends is let through.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.onKeyDown
functions.description: The panel's keys while it is open: arrows move the focus (Left/Right on a cycle row are the row's), Enter clicks, Back or Escape closes. Every key is kept from YouTube.

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.attach
functions.description: Starts handling keys (the panel opened).

functions.name: createPanelKeyboard.detach
functions.description: Stops handling keys (the panel closed).

functions.name: helpLine
functions.description: A line of small help text under a row.

functions.name: buildMainPage
functions.description: The Main page: Cosmetic Filtering (Ad Blocking and the filters that depend on it, greyed out while it is off), then the other features.

functions.name: buildMainPage.updateDependencyState
functions.description: Greys out the rows that depend on Ad Blocking while it is off.

functions.name: buildSponsorPage
functions.description: The SponsorBlock page: the switch, one row per category, and the SponsorBlock options.

functions.name: buildShortcutsPage
functions.description: The Shortcuts page: one row per configurable key.

functions.name: buildUITweaksPage
functions.description: The UI Tweaks page: shelf opacity, previews, titles, rows ahead, Liquid Glass, the theme, and the emoji fix on webOS 3/4.

functions.name: createDeferredBuilder
functions.description: The pages, built lazily into `container`: `elements[i]` is page i once built, `ensure(i)` builds it now, `startDeferred()` builds the rest one per animation frame. A builder never runs twice.

functions.name: createDeferredBuilder.ensure
functions.description: Builds page `index` now, if it is not built yet, and adds it to the panel.

functions.name: createDeferredBuilder.startDeferred
functions.description: Builds the pages not built yet, one per animation frame, so opening the panel does not wait for all of them.

functions.name: createDeferredBuilder.startDeferred.step
functions.description: Builds the next unbuilt page and asks for another frame.

functions.name: createTabMenu
functions.description: The tab bar: a button per page, the first one active; `onPick(index)` on a click, and the pointer leaving the bar puts focus back on the open tab (`activeIndex()`). Returns the bar and its buttons.

functions.name: isOptionsPanelVisible
functions.description: Whether the options panel is currently shown.

functions.name: createHeading
functions.description: The heading with the logo. A logo click (a Magic Remote pointer affordance; the logo is not in the focus order) flips the theme and hands focus back through `afterToggle`; the UI Theme row on the UI Tweaks page is the key path. There is one drawn logo per look (blue, red, dark): the <html> theme classes pick the one shown (panel.css, theme-red.css, theme-oled.css). A CSS filter on the blue image came out orange for red and too bright for OLED.

functions.name: createHeading.toggleTheme
functions.description: Switches to the next UI theme (a click on the logo).

functions.name: createHeading.logo
functions.description: One of the heading's logos (one per theme; CSS shows the current one); a click switches the theme.

functions.name: createOptionsPanel
functions.description: Builds the options panel: heading, tab bar, the Main page (the others are built later), the keyboard handler and the focus trap. Returns the element and its controls.

functions.name: createOptionsPanel.syncPopup
functions.description: Shows the SponsorBlock segment popup beside the panel while its page is open on a watch page.

functions.name: createOptionsPanel.setActivePage
functions.description: Shows page `pageIndex` (building it first if needed), marks its tab, and moves the focus into it unless the user is on the tab bar.

functions.name: createOptionsPanel.activeTab
functions.description: The tab button of the open page.

functions.name: showOptionsPanel
functions.description: Opens (building it the first time) or closes the options panel, with its keyboard handler, focus trap and popup. Toggles are ignored for 500 ms after the first build.

functions.name: window.ytaf_panelTakesToggles
functions.description: Test hook: whether the panel takes toggles again (the first build's 500 ms block is over).

functions.name: withSponsorBlock
functions.description: Runs `fn` with the live SponsorBlock handler, or says there is none.

functions.name: ACTIONS.config_menu.run
functions.description: Opens or closes the options panel, ending the OLED overlay first (it would cover the panel).

functions.name: ACTIONS.refresh_page.run
functions.description: Soft-reloads the page, except on a player page, where it only says it cannot.

functions.name: ACTIONS.toggle_subs.run
functions.description: The player lookup is here rather than in the router: only this action needs it, and the fallback is a full-document class-selector walk.

functions.name: ACTIONS.sb_skip_prev.run
functions.description: Jumps back to the start of the last SponsorBlock segment passed.

functions.name: ACTIONS.sb_manual_skip.run
functions.description: Skips the segment SponsorBlock is offering, or jumps to the highlight.

functions.name: updateShortcutCache
functions.description: Reads one binding. An action this build does not have (a binding stored by an older one) becomes None, in the cache and in the config, so the key is the app's again and the panel shows a value it knows; warned once, here.

functions.name: ensureMenuKey
functions.description: The settings must stay reachable: with no key bound to the menu, Green is bound to it again, said with `announce`. The key that opens the menu, and whether Green was just bound to it. Run at the start and whenever the panel closes (a binding changed on it may have unbound the menu).

functions.name: getKeyColor
functions.description: Colour-key code to name, alternates included, from REMOTE_KEYS in core/remote.js.

functions.name: simulateBack
functions.description: Sends the remote's Back key to YouTube.

functions.name: getEngagementPanel
functions.description: Engagement panel detection: whichever of the two shells exists.

functions.name: isEngagementPanelVisible
functions.description: Whether YouTube's engagement panel (comments, description) is on screen.

functions.name: announcePressed
functions.description: "<label>: ON" or "OFF" from the button's aria-pressed, once a click on it has taken effect (250 ms).

functions.name: triggerInternal
functions.description: Clicks a YouTube button, and calls its component's onSelect() when it has one.

functions.name: isOledOverlayActive
functions.description: Whether the black OLED overlay is showing.

functions.name: toggleOledOverlay
functions.description: The OLED black overlay with its keep-alive, toggled by the oled_toggle shortcut.

functions.name: refreshPage
functions.description: Asks YouTube to soft-reload the current page, with the same innertube command its own UI sends.

functions.name: firstMatch
functions.description: The first element a candidate selector finds, in the order given (a key press, a few lookups).

functions.name: isPressed
functions.description: Whether a toggle button shows as on (aria-pressed or aria-selected).

functions.name: togglePanelButton
functions.description: Toggles a panel: Back when `isOpen()` says it is up (or its button reads pressed), else a click on `button` with `onOpened` afterwards; a toast when there is no button to click.

functions.name: toggleComments
functions.description: Opens or closes the comments, or the live chat on a live stream; says so when neither is available.

functions.name: findDescriptionButton
functions.description: The description button, by its label text, else the generic text button.

functions.name: toggleDescription
functions.description: Opens or closes the description panel; once it is open, the dislike counter is asked to look for it.

functions.name: saveToPlaylist
functions.description: Opens or closes the Save (Watch Later, playlists) dialog.

functions.name: toggleSubtitles
functions.description: Turns the captions on (the first track) or off through the player's API, or by pressing the captions button when the API has no answer; a toast says the result.

functions.name: notifyPlayPause
functions.description: The play/pause toast, one at a time: a live one takes the new text.

functions.name: controlsFocused
functions.description: Whether YouTube's controls bar holds the focus.

functions.name: hideControlsAfterPause
functions.description: A pause brings the controls bar up. Unless it was up already, it is kept hidden for 750 ms with the shadows and the clock (ui/hide-controls.js) and, on the watch page with no side panel open, dismissed with a Back once it has taken the focus.

functions.name: playPause
functions.description: Plays or pauses `video`, with a toast; after a pause the player controls are hidden again.

functions.name: isTextBox
functions.description: Whether `el` takes typed text: a textarea, or an input other than a checkbox or a colour.

functions.name: keyNameOf
functions.description: The shortcut key a keydown stands for ('red', '3', ...), or null.

functions.name: inScope
functions.description: Whether the action may run on the current page.

functions.name: onKeyDown
functions.description: The shortcut router (capture phase, before YouTube): runs the action bound to the key, drops a repeat of the same press, and leaves the keys to the options panel while it is open (apart from the key that closes it).

functions.name: getChapterEls
functions.description: The chapter markers on the progress bar, empty until the player UI has drawn them; the track's other children (the playhead, the buffer) are left out.

functions.name: dismissForcedUI
functions.description: The player UI was forced open for the markers; close it again once the seek is in.

functions.name: skipChapter
functions.description: Skips to the next or previous chapter; one skip at a time, never on Shorts.

functions.name: readChapters
functions.description: The chapter widths off the bar's markers, and their sum (0 when none has a width).

functions.name: pickChapterTarget
functions.description: Where the skip lands, or -1: forward, the first chapter starting more than a second past the playhead; back, the start of the current chapter, or of the one before it within the first three seconds of the current one.

functions.name: doSkipChapter
functions.description: Reads the chapters from the progress bar (showing the player UI first when they are not rendered), then seeks to the next or previous one.

functions.name: performBurstSeek
functions.description: One press of a burst: the toast shows the running total at once, the video is moved by the pending part once the presses pause for 200 ms (a seek per press froze the UI), and a change of direction starts the toast's total over; the part not applied yet still counts. The reset 1.2 s later ends only the toast's total: the part not applied yet is the seek timer's, and a stalled event loop may run the two in either order.

functions.name: read
functions.description: The current values of `keys`, as an object.

functions.name: syncOledShelfOpacity
functions.description: The shelf backdrop's opacity, written as a rule of its own rather than a custom property: Chromium 38 (webOS 3) has no var(). Written only while OLED-care mode is on: the rule selects on html.ytaf-oled, so without the mode it would be a stylesheet for nothing.

functions.name: initHtmlClasses
functions.description: Sets every class of HTML_CLASSES on <html> from its settings and keeps it in step, and writes the OLED shelf opacity rule.

functions.name: initHtmlClasses.sync
functions.description: Sets or removes one class from the current values of its settings.

functions.name: ensureContainer
functions.description: The toast container, created on first use.

functions.name: Toast.constructor
functions.description: Shows a toast with `text`: added hidden and faded in two frames later, removed after `time` ms (0: stays until removed).

functions.name: Toast.isLive
functions.description: Still on screen and not fading out. A flag rather than the hidden class: a new toast carries the class for its first two frames, and a repeat of its text in that window must extend it, not stack a twin.

functions.name: Toast.arm
functions.description: Restarts the removal timer (`time` 0: none).

functions.name: Toast.unkey
functions.description: Drops this toast from the by-text map, if it is still the one there.

functions.name: Toast.update
functions.description: New text, or the same text with a fresh timer; false once the toast is fading out.

functions.name: Toast.remove
functions.description: Fades the toast out and removes it a second later; frees its slot and its text.

functions.name: showNotification
functions.description: Shows `text` for `time` ms (0 keeps it up); returns a handle with remove(). With a `slot`, the toast that holds it takes the new text, unless it is already fading out.
